description: Core threat registry for the two prototype-anchor types (gate G6). Pruning rule R36/§2.12: every entry here is MECHANICAL — it owns balance numbers and changes the player's verb, not just the noun. Demoted codex flavour (stream-sniper, competitor-sponsored attack, hype-cycle-collapse-as-text) attaches to these entries later and does not ship stats. Second Answer rule (§5.1): every threat lists >=2 viable counters at DIFFERENT prices (cheap / expensive / lateral triad). Counters name the 9 defense roles (Absorb, Classify, Meter, Contain, Detect, Recover, Deter, Divert, Negotiate, §2.1). Stats are null + _todo wherever hosting_game.md is qualitative — the loader lint must flag each TODO until the tuning sheet is ratified (owner pick A/B/C pending, OD-2).

stats._todo: §2.2 authors behaviour (flags advance telegraph for the next 3 levels' targeted attacks) without stat scalars.

facts: Constant drizzle; renders violet (§2.2).
Telegraph function: each scanner that lands pre-announces the next three levels' targeted attacks — the attack-surface ledger's teacher (§2.2, gate G1).

stats._todo: §2.2 gives damage basis (CPU: full app bootstrap per attempt; log storage cost) but no stat scalars.

facts: Slow, relentless guessing at /wp-login.php; every attempt boots the whole app — damage is CPU plus log storage, not bandwidth (§2.2).

stats._todo: §2.2 authors the chain (your server attacks someone else -> abuse notice -> null-route threat) without scalars.

facts: Turns your fleet into the weapon: xmlrpc pingback flood launched FROM customer sites; the damage clock is the transit/upstream relationship, not the box (§2.2).

stats._todo: §2.3 authors near-zero bandwidth and thread-hold semantics without scalars.

facts: A handful of visitors sit forever holding worker threads; graphs look fine while the box dies — defeats bandwidth-based detection (§2.3).

counters.name: l7-req-rate-limit
counters.note: RUDY variant defeats naive request-rate limits (§2.3).

stats._todo: §2.4 authors behaviour + counter economics without stat scalars.

facts: Requests the most expensive page at human-plausible rates from thousands of residential IPs — indistinguishable from popularity; rate-limiting it craters conversion (§2.4).
One outdated CMS plugin popped -> mass defacement on EVERY account on the box + blocklisting of the whole IP range; homogeneity is the multiplier (§2.5, Matrix A signature threat).
Control-panel RCE is the fatal event: roots every box simultaneously (§0.3).

counters.name: managed-patching-service
counters.note: occasionally breaks a customer site — you own the outage either way (§2.5).

stats._todo: §3.1 gives the unindexed-DB latency band 400-4,000ms ('the Noisy Query's weapon'); the per-incident pressure scalar is untuned.

facts: A query that was fine at 10k rows is fatal at 10M — the threat grows with your success (§2.5).

Signature moment (§1.3): one customer's plugin runs an uncached SELECT * FROM wp_posts on every page load and takes down all 40 tenants; attributable only if the per-account slow-query-log buildable exists.

stats._todo: §2.9 gives the formula shape (tickets ∝ severity × customers × communication-quality-lag) without coefficients.

facts: Tickets consume staff, staff-absence extends the incident, the incident breeds tickets — the doom loop; the purest Attention-damage threat (§2.9).
'The enemy is sometimes a client' — you cannot evict the paying bad customer (§1.3 tutorial twist).

stats._todo: 40x fair share and 60% of box I/O are doc'd §2.10 verbatim; the churn-curve they drive is untuned.

facts: Customer using 40x fair share — a find / every minute; 60% of the box's I/O degrading 200 neighbours invisibly until churn (§2.10).
Visual 'The Elbow': one window swells and shoves the neighbours smaller (§2.10).
One account's find / is everyone's outage (§1.3).

counters.name: quota-policy-cgroups-lve
counters.note: POLICY answer, not a box answer (§2.10).

counters.name: enforce-limits
counters.note: enforcement breeds angry churn + bad review (§2.10).

stats._todo: Grudge per-archetype 0-5 is doc'd (§2.24); booter price-per-hour economics are codex in §2.12.

facts: Aimed at a single player's session over a grudge; collaterally kills the whole server everyone else is on (§2.12).
Popularity is a targeting beacon — the best server is the one under attack (§1.3).
Counter costs LATENCY, the thing you sell (§2.12).

counters.name: per-player-ip-obfuscation-proxy
counters.note: the named counter (§2.12) — pays in milliseconds of the scarce resource.

counters.name: udp-aware-ddos-scrubbing
counters.note: cannot just drop UDP — it IS the game protocol (§1.3).

stats._todo: 50x multiplier and ~10s telegraph are doc'd §2.3; pipe-size balance untuned.

facts: 50x multiplier; a slow wall that doesn't path — the pipe is the victim; telegraphed ~10s ahead (§2.3).
Must be DIVERTED upstream: scrubbing retainer, anycast, BGP flowspec, bigger transit; cheap early option RTBH blackhole = sacrifice one address (§2.3).

counters.name: anycast
counters.note: learned in the DNS level (§1.3 returning hook).

stats._todo: §2.3/§1.3 author the chain; NTP/DNS/memcached per-protocol gain factors unauthored.

facts: YOUR servers (open NTP/DNS/memcached) are the reflectors against someone else; you take no damage — then the abuse complaint, the transit spike, the null-route threat (§2.3).
Game flavour (§1.3): UDP amplification reflection where your servers are the reflectors.

stats._todo: §2.12 authors the friction trade (anti-cheat costs tick performance and bans innocents) without scalars.

facts: An attack on the game your customer hosts — damages customer happiness, not infrastructure; customers blame YOU (§2.12).
Visual: a pawn animating the wrong frames; other pawns turn to look, then leave the lobby (§2.12).

counters.name: anti-cheat-integration
counters.note: costs tick performance; false bans are friction applied to reputation (§2.12).

counters.name: community-moderation-tools
counters.note: customer-side admins with ban power (§1.3 Private Shard texture).

stats._todo: 'breaks 900 instances at once' (§1.3) is doc'd; the failure-cascade curve is untuned.

facts: A dependency you don't own breaks every instance at a time chosen by someone else (§2.12).
The modding community is simultaneously your best marketing and your worst attack surface (§2.12, Matrix B game deck).

counters.name: staged-version-pinning
counters.note: roll mods to a canary pool first — counters derived provisionally from §1.3 buildables.

stats._todo: §2.12 KEEP-LIST entry (visitors affecting visitors — the named mechanical exception); the population threshold below which the spiral becomes terminal is untuned.

facts: Below the population threshold a server empties and never recovers: full attracts, empty repels (§2.12, §3.3 herding law).
Delayed bounce: a bad session doesn't just lose a player, it makes the lobby visibly emptier for the next one (§3.3).

counters.name: server-browser-listing-placement
counters.note: buys visibility against the repulsion — counters provisional; doc authors the spiral, not its cures.

counters.name: launch-event-escort
counters.note: the Escort scenario (§3.3 tournament) re-fills the room.

stats._todo: 'chargebacks 2-4% of revenue' + stolen-card signups doc'd §1.3/§2.10; fraud-mix scalars untuned.

facts: Fraud is endemic: stolen-card signups, chargebacks at 2-4% of revenue; kids with allowances on card-verifiable terms (§1.3, §2.10).
Cash denomination pressure that no defense box absorbs — it arrives through the payment rail.

counters.note: monthly-prepay tempo already biases this way (§6.6 companion A).
